title: UGREEN’s smart home hubs put an AI data center in your kitchen to protect your privacy
summary: Putting privacy on a pedestal — if you can afford it.
body: TL;DR UGREEN is launching three smart home hubs that combine network storage, video recording, and local AI processing. Instead of talking to Gemini in the cloud like you do with Google Home, here all voice commands are processed by the hub itself. Depending on your needs, UGREEN’s hardware can offer some seriously heavy-duty NVIDIA AI silicon. Smart homes are getting smarter, and that might just be a problem. While the idea of a more feature-reach, accessible, and proactive smart home sounds great on face value, the growing reliance of so many of these systems on cloud-based AI is making some shoppers think twice. UGREEN believes it might just have the solution in the form of some advanced smart home hubs. Ecosystems like Google Home tap into cloud-powered AI continually, from processing your voice input, to analyzing your Nest camera footage. Beyond obvious privacy considerations, there’s also the subscription cost to consider with the more advanced camera functionality, to say nothing of storage.

title: You can now talk your way through Gmail, Docs, and Keep
summary: Gemini can now turn your voice into answers, documents, and organized notes.
body: TL;DR Gmail, Docs, and Keep can now understand natural voice commands and turn them into useful actions. Docs Live can pull info from Gmail, Drive, Chat, and the web, while Keep Live organizes free-flowing thoughts into notes and lists. The new voice features are rolling out now to eligible Google AI subscribers, with Workspace support coming soon. Back at Google I/O, the company showed how Gemini could make Gmail, Docs, and Keep feel less like apps you operate and more like assistants you talk to. The company promised that these new voice-powered experiences would be available this summer, and after a few early glimpses , the wait is finally over. Gmail Live, Docs Live, and Keep Live are rolling out now, giving users new ways to get things done without reaching for the keyboard. Gmail Live is perhaps the most immediately useful of the three. Instead of digging through your inbox or remembering the right keywords, you can ask a question out loud. Gmail can connect information across emails to synthesize an answer. That could mean asking when your kid’s next school event is, checking an order update, or finding information buried across multiple messages.

title: Flowtica Verso snaps onto your phone with an e-paper display for AI-powered meeting notes
summary: You can check your meeting action items right on the back of your phone, no app needed.
body: TL;DR The Flowtica Verso is a MagSafe-compatible AI companion with an e-paper touchscreen that gives you direct access to meeting summaries, calendars, and action items. The device comes with 64GB of storage, up to 72 hours of battery life, a couple of physical buttons for controlling key functions, and a non-disableable LED recording indicator. The Flowtica Verso costs $299 and will ship in Q4 2026. The AI hardware space is evolving beyond screenless pins and clip-on wearables . While existing devices like the PLAUD NotePin focus on discreet voice capture that relies entirely on a companion smartphone app, Flowtica is taking a different approach. Unveiled at IFA 2026, the newly announced Flowtica Verso is a magnetic AI companion that snaps onto the back of your smartphone and features an always-on e-paper display to keep your summaries, schedules, and AI insights visible at a glance. Unlike traditional AI voice recorders that act as screenless “black boxes,” the Flowtica Verso delivers its core experience directly on the hardware. It integrates a 259ppi e-paper touchscreen that keeps meeting summaries, calendars, and action items visible without forcing you to open a mobile app.

title: The weather app on your Pixel Watch is adding new watch face modules
summary: The Pixel Weather app for Wear OS is gaining three new watch face complications, taking the tally to six.
body: TL;DR A new Pixel Weather update for Wear OS introduces three new complications. Pixel Watch owners can now add Air quality index, Pollen, and Precipitation complications to their watch face. Some third-party Wear OS weather apps already offer some of these complications for Pixel Watch owners. Google retired the existing Weather app for Pixel Watch models last year in favor of the Pixel Weather app . Since then, the app has allowed Pixel Watch owners to choose from up to three watch face complications: Sunrise and sunset, UV Index, and Weather. Now, a new Pixel Weather update for Wear OS is adding three more complications to the list. Google is rolling out dedicated complications for Air quality index, Pollen, and Precipitation as part of the version 1.0.0.94 update of the Pixel Weather app. For the uninitiated, complications on smartwatches are like widgets that offer information in real time on the watch face. Common complications on the Pixel Watch include battery level, a step counter, and upcoming calendar appointments.

title: Eye-friendly NXTPAPER or an OLED screen? TCL’s new US-bound phones don’t force you to choose
summary: These are the first phones to pair NXTPAPER tech with OLED screens, and the Ultra has a nifty camera system too.
body: Credit: Paul Jones / Android Authority TL;DR TCL has announced the P80 series of smartphones. The TCL 80 Pro and Ultra both have NXTPAPER OLED screens, while the Ultra also has a 50MP 3x camera. The phones start at ~$404, but you’ll need to spend at least ~$496 if you want a model with NXTPAPER. TCL has been producing NXTPAPER phones for a while now, offering a glare-free display compared to typical Android smartphones . Now, the company has announced the TCL P80 series at IFA 2026. The P80 Ultra and P80 Pro have plenty of features in common. For one, there’s the 6.83-inch OLED NXTPAPER display (1.5K, 120Hz, 3,200 nits peak brightness). TCL says these are the first phones to feature NXTPAPER paired with an OLED screen instead of an LCD panel. The NXTPAPER tech reduces glare and reflections for a more pleasant viewing experience. There’s also a NXTPAPER button that activates a Max Ink Mode. This mode turns your screen into a monochrome display, akin to an E-Ink panel. In fact, TCL claims up to seven days of reading in this mode.

title: Google Chrome just gave its Gemini side panel a feature it should’ve had years ago
summary: Gemini in Chrome can finally sink its AI teeth into your files.
body: TL;DR Chrome’s Gemini side panel is finally gaining the ability to upload files directly through the Add attachments menu. You can hand Gemini a document and ask it to summarize, explain, or find specific information without leaving Chrome. It’s a useful addition, but Google is surprisingly late to the party, as Microsoft Edge’s Copilot sidebar has supported file uploads for years. Gemini has been steadily working its way into just about every corner of Google’s ecosystem . You can summon it across Google apps , use it on Android phones , and even have it sitting alongside whatever you’re doing in Chrome. But despite all of that integration, the Gemini side panel in Chrome has been missing a surprisingly basic feature: the ability to upload a file. That finally appears to be changing. X user Leopeva64 spotted a new file upload option inside the Gemini side panel in Chrome, tucked under the Add attachments menu. title: The Fairphone Gen 6 Plus is everything an Android phone should be — and no one will buy it
summary: Built fairly, built to last. Tough to sell.
body: Every year — or maybe every other year — we all have one thing in common: we shop for a new phone. Phone makers know that even when sales are in a slump, there will be millions of eyeballs looking at what’s out there and what the market has to offer. The flashier and “louder” a product or feature is, the more attention it grabs and the more sales it generates. Even if you didn’t buy a Samsung foldable, you might have bought another Galaxy phone you saw while shopping. Sometimes though, it doesn’t work that way, and the lack of fanfare doesn’t drive all those eyeballs to a product or manufacturer.
